references.text: God does not see as man sees; man looks at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart ([ref:1 Sam 16:7|1 Samuel 16:7]). This corresponds directly to Jesus' words that God knows the hearts, in contrast to what is highly regarded among men.

"Every man thinks his way is right, but the Lord weighs the hearts" ([ref:Ordsp 21:2|Proverbs 21:2]). Parallel to the idea that people justify themselves, but God knows the true condition of the heart.
"He who is proud in heart is an abomination to the Lord" ([ref:Ordsp 16:5|Proverbs 16:5]). What is highly esteemed among men is an abomination (βδέλυγμα) to God – the same thought as in Luke 16:15.
"God tests the hearts and kidneys" ([ref:Sal 7:10|Psalms 7:10]). God's knowledge of man's inner being confirms Jesus' statement that God knows the hearts.
"I, the Lord, search the heart and test the kidneys" ([ref:Jer 17:10|Jeremiah 17:10]). A central Old Testament declaration about God's ability to know the human heart, which Jesus refers to here.
The parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector ([ref:Luk 18:9-14|Luke 18:9-14]) illustrates exactly how people justify themselves before others, but God sees differently.

Jesus calls the Pharisees "whitewashed tombs" that outwardly appear righteous to men, but inwardly are full of hypocrisy ([ref:Matt 23:27-28|Matthew 23:27-28]). This expresses the same idea as them justifying themselves before men.

Paul writes that a true Jew is one in secret, and circumcision is of the heart – "his praise is not from men but from God" ([ref:Rom 2:29|Romans 2:29]). The contrast between human and divine judgment reflects Jesus' words.
Paul says he does not speak to be approved by men, but by God "who tests our hearts" ([ref:1 Tess 2:4|1 Thessalonians 2:4]). The same contrast between human approval and God's knowledge of the heart.

"My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways" ([ref:Jes 55:8-9|Isaiah 55:8-9]). God's values are radically different from man's, just as what is highly esteemed among men is an abomination to God.
Among the things the Lord hates are proud eyes and a lying heart ([ref:Ordsp 6:16-17|Proverbs 6:16-17]). What people value highly – pride and self-assertion – is an abomination to God.
